Single-premium annuities: one deposit, a fixed rate or lifetime payments

A single-premium annuity is bought with one deposit instead of ongoing contributions. Depending on the type, it pays a fixed interest rate for a set number of years or turns a lump sum into payments for life.

Reviewed by Luay Sadqi, Licensed Agent · NPN 21370662 · Updated November 2026

Schedule an appointment Call (301) 615-8289

The three main types

TypeWhat it doesOften used for
MYGA (multi-year guaranteed annuity)Pays a fixed interest rate for a set term, commonly 3 to 10 years, with interest tax-deferredMoney from a maturing CD or savings you will not need for a few years
SPIA (single-premium immediate annuity)Converts a lump sum into payments that start within a year, for life or a set periodCovering fixed bills in retirement
Single-premium fixed indexed annuityCredits interest by an index formula with a floor, usually over a longer termLonger-term money, sometimes with an income rider

How a MYGA compares with a CD

  • Tax. MYGA interest is not taxed until you withdraw it. CD interest is taxed each year.
  • Backing. A CD is FDIC-insured up to the legal limit. An annuity is backed by the claims-paying ability of the insurance company.
  • Access. Most MYGAs allow limited withdrawals each year. Taking more before the term ends triggers surrender charges.
  • Age rule. Earnings withdrawn before age 59½ are generally subject to a 10% federal tax penalty on top of income tax.
Read this before you buy: An annuity is a long-term contract, not a savings account. Surrender charges apply if you take out more than the contract allows during the term. Rates and features vary by carrier and state, and guarantees depend on the insurer's claims-paying ability. Keep money you may need soon somewhere you can reach it.

Where the money can come from

Savings and maturing CDs, an old 401(k) or IRA through a direct rollover, the Thrift Savings Plan for federal employees, or an existing annuity or life policy through a 1035 exchange. How it is moved determines whether tax is owed, so we handle transfers directly between institutions.

Who a single-premium annuity fits

  • People within about ten years of retirement, or already retired, who want part of their savings out of the market
  • Savers comparing CD renewal rates
  • Retirees who want a payment they cannot outlive to cover essentials

It does not fit money you may need for emergencies, and it should rarely be all of your savings.

Common questions

Single-Premium Annuities FAQ

What is a MYGA?
A multi-year guaranteed annuity pays a fixed interest rate for a set term, commonly 3 to 10 years. Interest is tax-deferred, and withdrawals above the contract allowance during the term are subject to surrender charges.
Is an annuity as safe as a CD?
They are protected differently. CDs are FDIC-insured up to the legal limit. Annuities are backed by the claims-paying ability of the insurer.
Can I roll my 401(k) or IRA into an annuity without paying tax?
A direct rollover or transfer from a 401(k) or IRA into an IRA annuity is generally not a taxable event. The details depend on the account type, so confirm with a tax professional.
What if I need the money early?
Most contracts allow a limited withdrawal each year without a charge. Larger withdrawals during the term trigger surrender charges, and earnings taken before age 59 and a half generally face a 10% federal tax penalty.
